analysis.title: USD Rates Chart Pack: Futures Positions & Curve Analysis
key_insights: Non-commercial net positions in Treasury futures are net short across every contract: TU -856.8K, FV -1,074.1K, TY -964.3K, UXY -149.3K, US -68.4K, WN -375.2K.

As of 10/20/2026, asset managers are long and leveraged accounts are short in the 2Y, 5Y, 10Y, Ultra-10Y and Bond Treasury futures, with the largest leveraged shorts in the 5Y (-2,107.2K) and 10Y (-2,117.5K) contracts.
In the 2Y contract asset managers hold +849.4K, dealers -93.4K, leveraged -804.8K and others +40.5K as of 10/20/2026.

Positioning in Fed funds and SOFR futures is split. Non-commercial 3M SOFR is net short -2,415.3K and 30-day Fed funds net long +307.3K. Leveraged accounts are -2,373.0K in 3M SOFR while dealers are +2,628.8K.
Non-commercial E-mini S&P 500 is net short -142.7K and Nasdaq 100 mini net long +50.7K.
The swap curve flattened from 10/19 to 10/23/2026. 2s10s fell from 11.8 to 6.1bp, 2s30s from 21.0 to 14.1bp and 2s5s from 2.6 to -1.1bp, so 2s5s is now inverted.
The Treasury curve also flattened over the same week. 2s10s fell from 36.6 to 30.5bp, 2s30s from 70.3 to 63.1bp and 5s30s from 53.7 to 50.5bp.
Treasury 2s10s at 30.5bp and 2s30s at 63.1bp sit well below their long-run averages of 56.87bp and 90.40bp. Swap 2s10s at 6.1bp is also below its 2.53bp-average-based range.
The report notes that extreme positioning and curvature may lead to near-term rate or curve changes, and that a high butterfly spread (long the belly) means the belly is cheap versus the wings.
Swap 10-20-30 butterfly is 11.2 and Treasury 10-20-30 butterfly is 20.9 as of 10/23/2026. Treasury 5-10-30 is -7.2.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 11.8bp on 10/19, a flattening of the swap curve over the week.
Down from 36.6bp on 10/19 and below the 56.87bp long-run average.
Down from 70.3bp on 10/19 and below the 90.40bp long-run average.

vol_and_positioning: CFTC non-commercial net positions in Treasury futures are net short in all six contracts (TU, FV, TY, UXY, US, WN).

Leveraged accounts are short and asset managers long in most Treasury futures as of 10/20/2026. Leveraged net is -2,107.2K in 5Y and -2,117.5K in 10Y against asset managers at +2,925.4K and +2,928.1K.
Dealers are net short in all six Treasury futures but net long in 3M SOFR (+2,628.8K) and Fed funds (+235.0K) per the trader-type tables.
3M SOFR non-commercial net is -2,415.3K, 30-day Fed funds is +307.3K, 1M SOFR is 0.0K.
